\[(x_1,y_1)=(0,-2),(x_2,y_2)=(6,-5)\]So \[\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2},\frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{0+6}{2},\frac{-2+(-5)}2\right)=\left(\frac62,-\frac72\right)=\left(3,-\frac72\right)\]Substitute \(x=3\) and \(y=-\frac72\) into \(x-2y-10=0\):\[(3)-2\left(-\frac72\right)-10=3+7-10=0\]So the centre is on the line \(x-2y-10=0\).

5 Point \(X\) has coordinates \((7,-2)\) and point \(Y\) has coordinates \((4,q)\). The perpendicular bisector of \(XY\) has equation \(y=4x+b\). Find the value of \(q\) and the value of \(b\).

\(X(7,-2)\) and \(Y(4,q)\)\[\text{The gradient of the line segment }XY=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}=\frac{q-(-2)}{4-7}=\frac{q+2}{-3}\]From the equation of the perpendicular bisector of PQ, \(y=4x+b\), the gradient is 4. Therefore, the gradient of \(XY=-\frac14\), so \(-\frac14=\frac{q+2}{-3}\).\[q=-\frac54\]\[\text{Midpoint of }XY=\left(\frac{7+4}2,\frac{-2+(-\frac54)}2\right)=\left(\frac{11}2,-\frac{13}8\right)\]Substituting \(x=\frac{11}2\) and \(y=-\frac{13}8\) into \(y=4x+b\) gives\[-\frac{13}8=4\left(\frac{11}2\right)+b,\qquad b=-\frac{189}8\]So \(b=-\frac{189}8,\ q=-\frac54\).

blocks.tex: 6 a Show that the line \(x+y=11\) meets the circle with equation \(x^2+(y-3)^2=32\) at only one point. \hfill\(\text{(4 mar}\ldots\)\par b Find the coordinates of the point of intersection. \hfill\(\text{(1 ma}\ldots\)

\textbf{a} Rearranging \(x+y=11\)\[y=11-x\]Substitute \(y=11-x\) into \(x^2+(y-3)^3=32\).\[\begin{aligned}x^2+((11-x)-3)^2&=32\\x^2+(11-x-3)^2&=32\\x^2+(8-x)^2&=32\\x^2+64-16x+x^2&=32\\2x^2-16x+64&=32\\2x^2-16x+32&=0\\x^2-8x+16&=0\\(x-4)(x-4)&=0\end{aligned}\]The line meets the circle at \(x=4\) (only). So the line is a tangent.
\textbf{b} Substitute \(x=4\) into \(y=11-x\)\[\begin{aligned}y&=11-(4)\\y&=11-4\\y&=7\end{aligned}\]The point of intersection is \((4,7)\).

blocks.tex: 6 The tangent to the circle \((x+4)^2+(y-1)^2=242\) at \((7,-10)\) meets the \(y\)-axis at \(S\) and the \(x\)-axis at \(T\).\par a Find the coordinates of \(S\) and \(T\). \hfill(5 marks)\par b Hence, find the area of \(\triangle OST\), where \(O\) is the origin. \hfill(3 marks)

\textbf{a} The centre of the circle \((x+4)^2+(y-1)^2=242\) is \((-4,1)\). The gradient of the line joining \((-4,1)\) and \((7,-10)\) is\[\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}=\frac{-10-1}{7-(-4)}=\frac{-11}{7+4}=-\frac{11}{11}=-1\]The gradient of the tangent is \(\frac{-1}{(-1)}=1\).
The equation of the tangent is\[\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1)\\y-(-10)&=1(x-7)\\y+10&=x-7\\y&=x-17\end{aligned}\]

Substitute \(x=0\) into \(y=x-17\)\[\begin{aligned}y&=0-17\\y&=-17\end{aligned}\]So the coordinates of \(S\) are \((0,-17)\).\par Substitute \(y=0\) into \(y=x-17\)\[\begin{aligned}0&=x-17\\x&=17\end{aligned}\]So the coordinates of \(T\) are \((17,0)\).

\textbf{a} \[M=\left(\frac{2+10}2,\frac{3+1}2\right)=(6,2)\]\[\text{Gradient }RS=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}=\frac{1-3}{10-2}=-\frac14\]Gradient of \(l\) is 4.\[\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1)\\y-2&=4(x-6)\\y&=4x-22\text{ is the equation of }l\end{aligned}\]\textbf{b} Using \(y=4x-22\) when \(x=a,y=-2\):\[-2=4a-22,\ a=5\]
\textbf{c} \[\text{radius}=\text{distance }CR=\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}=\sqrt{(2-5)^2+(3-(-2))^2}=\sqrt{34}\]Centre of circle is \((5,-2)\).\par Equation of circle is \((x-5)^2+(y+2)^2=34\).

\textbf{d} Solve \(y=4x-22\) and \((x-5)^2+(y+2)^2=34\) simultaneously.\[\begin{aligned}(x-5)^2+(4x-20)^2&=34\\x^2-10x+25+16x^2-160x+400-34&=0\\17x^2-170x+391&=0\\x^2-10x+23&=0\end{aligned}\]Using the formula, \(x=\frac{10\pm\sqrt8}2=5\pm\sqrt2\).\par When \(x=5+\sqrt2,\ y=4(5+\sqrt2)-22=-2+4\sqrt2\).\par When \(x=5-\sqrt2,\ y=4(5-\sqrt2)-22=-2-4\sqrt2\).\par \(A(5+\sqrt2,-2+4\sqrt2)\) and \(B(5-\sqrt2,-2-4\sqrt2)\).

9 A circle has equation \(x^2+2x+y^2-24y-24=0\).\par a Find the centre and radius of the circle.\par b The points \(A(-13,17)\) and \(B(11,7)\) both lie on the circumference of the circle. Show that \(AB\) is a diameter of the circle.\par c The point \(C\) lies on the negative \(x\)-axis and the angle \(ACB=90^\circ\). Find the coordinates of \(C\).

\textbf{a} \(x^2+2x+y^2-24y-24=0\). Completing the square gives:\[\begin{aligned}(x+1)^2-1+(y-12)^2-144-24&=0\\(x+1)^2+(y-12)^2&=169\end{aligned}\]Centre of the circle is \((-1,12)\) and the radius of the circle is 13.\par\textbf{b} If \(AB\) is the diameter of the circle then the midpoint of AB is the centre of the circle.\[\text{Midpoint of }AB=\left(\frac{-13+11}2,\frac{17+7}2\right)=(-1,12)\]Therefore, \(AB\) is the diameter of the circle.\par\textbf{c} The point \(C\) lies on the \(x\)-axis, so \(y=0\). Substitute \(y=0\) into the equation of the circle.\[\begin{aligned}(x+1)^2+(0-12)^2&=169\\x^2+2x+1+144&=169\\x^2+2x-24&=0\\(x+6)(x-4)&=0\\x=-6,\quad x&=4\end{aligned}\]As \(x\) is negative, \(x=-6\). The coordinates of \(C\) are \((-6,0)\).
